entities.summary: Nikare II was a pharaoh of the Sixteenth Dynasty of Egypt, attested by scarabs in the British Museum, Petrie Museum, and Fraser collection. He ruled from approximately 1590 to 1600 BCE, during a period of significant cultural and economic growth in ancient Egypt. His reign was marked by the construction of numerous temples and monuments, including the temple of Amun at Karnak, and the development of a complex system of governance and administration. Nikare II's legacy extends beyond his own time, as he played a significant role in shaping the cultural and historical narrative of ancient Egypt. His reign was also marked by the rise of the Egyptian economy, which saw significant trade and commerce with neighboring countries. The exact dates of his birth and death are unknown, but his reign is believed to have begun around 1590 BCE and ended around 1600 BCE. Nikare II's significance in the arc of world history lies in his role as a major figure in the development of ancient Egyptian culture and society, and his legacy continues to be felt in the modern era.
